train:
Bring one steady hand to the mouth of my cave
I'll drum with the other seven under the wave.

Try keeping a beat on a shell in the sand
I'll play seven more without asking for a hand.

Take your best hook to the end of the pier
I'll send it back twice so the whole bay can hear.

Can you open a jar while the tide pulls you wide?
I'll spin the lid loose with a snare on each side.

Bring your loudest drum to the edge of the reef
I'll play eight together and keep the solo brief.

Try catching my verse in a basket of rope
I'll slip through the weave on a ribbon of hope.

Bring a bright lantern to the mouth of the deep
I'll write with my ink while the last fish sleep.

Can you tie eight knots in one length of line?
I'll leave seven loose and make the last one mine.

Try following my footsteps to the side of a wreck
I'll tap out the rhythm from below the deck.

Bring your next chorus to a rock in the bay
I'll braid it with kelp before it floats away.

Try reading my verse by the moon on the sea
I'll ink out eight bars and leave one for thee.

Bring a brass bell to the floor of the blue
I'll make eight shells ring and send one back to you.

Can you play through the current when the water goes cold?
I'll warm up the groove with the shells that I hold.

Try running this stage with just one pair of feet
I'll lay down a rhythm that can stand on eight beats.

Bring one tangled hook to the rim of my den
I'll work it loose and tie it tighter again.

Try keeping up when the whitecaps fly
I'll send up a spray that puts salt in the sky.

Bring your whole band to a rock by the shore
I'll give you eight rhythms when you ask for four.

Can you keep the same beat through a tunnel of stone?
I'll drum with all eight and make it my own.

Try reading a line through a curtain of ink
I'll change up the rhythm before you can blink.

Bring your next verse to the mouth of the creek
I'll send back the bass before you can speak.

Try counting the arms that come out of my lair
I'll keep half on the snare and the rest in the air.

Bring your best beat to the middle of the night
I'll keep time with shells where there isn't a light.

Try landing a punchline from the back of a whale
I'll drum on the deck while the wind fills the sail.

Bring your best rhyme to the edge of the foam
I'll ride the last wave and carry it home.

Try putting your chorus inside of a chest
I'll lift all the latches and give it a rest.

Bring a tin drum to the place where I dwell
I'll give you a rhythm from inside a shell.

Try slipping a beat through a net full of holes
I'll send it around with a drum made of bowls.

Bring a slow song to the bed of the stream
I'll make eight arms move like a dance in a dream.
validation:
Try tapping a rhythm on the rim of a dish
I'll echo it back through a whole school of fish.

Bring your best hook to the end of the track
I'll spin it with eight arms and throw it right back.

Try playing your solo where the sunlight dies
I'll lift up the beat while the cold bubbles rise.

Bring your sharpest jab to a nook in the wall
I'll dodge with eight arms and keep time through it all.
